why: `=` on a `number` compares numerically, so `length_km=7.0` matches the reach that wrote `7`. As text it matches nothing. The rule exists so that `<`, `=` and `>` stay trichotomous on a number: a server that ordered numerically and compared equality as text would have a value in none of the three, and `=`'s date rule — match at the precision the query wrote — has no analogue here because `7` and `7.0` denote one point where `1893` denotes an interval. `~` stays textual on every type, so `length_km~7` reads the digits.
